Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County
A weeklong festival in April that features hundreds of independent films. It is one of the largest film festivals in the Southern United States.

A citywide event typically held in March or April, this is a celebration of Nashville's fashion and retail community featuring local, regional and national design talent in fashion events and shows. [ 221 ]
Marathon, half marathon, and 5k race held in April with runners from around the world. In 2012, participation surpassed 30,000 runners.

A two-day music festival held every April at Vanderbilt University since 1986. Rites of Spring has welcomed a number of famous artists to the Vanderbilt campus, including Wiz Khalifa, Young the Giant, Drake, Steve Aoki, and the Red Hot Chili Peppers. [ 222 ]
Annual steeplechase horse racing event held in May at Percy Warner Park.
A four-day event in June featuring performances by country music stars, autograph signings, artist/fan interaction, and other activities for country music fans.

A two-day event held in June that fosters awareness of and for the LGBT community and culture in Middle Tennessee. The 2019 festival drew a record crowd of over 75,000 people, establishing it as the largest LGBT event in Tennessee. [ 223 ]

Held every Fourth of July at Riverfront Park, featuring a street festival and live music, and culminating in one of the largest fireworks shows in the country. [ 224 ] An estimated 280,000 people attended the 2014 celebration. [ 225 ]
Held each August in East Nashville, this event celebrates the Tomato as a Unifier. [ 226 ]
Held in September on the campus of Tennessee State University. It is committed to connecting and celebrating the extensions of Africa to America. [ 227 ]
Live on the Green Music Festival
A free concert series held in August and September at Public Square Park by local radio station Lightning 100.
The State Fair held in September at the State Fairgrounds, which lasts nine days and includes rides, exhibits, rodeos, tractor pulls, and numerous other shows and attractions.

A free event held the first Saturday in October at Centennial Park, it is Middle Tennessee's largest multicultural festival and includes music and dance performances, ethnic food court, children's area, teen area, and marketplace. [ 228 ]
An annual Art Fair in downtown Nashville. Includes galleries and dealers from around the world. Open to the public. [ 229 ]

A free event held in the historic Germantown neighborhood since 1980 celebrating the culture and customs of Germany. [ 230 ] Oktoberfest is Nashville's oldest annual festival and is one of the largest in the South. [ 231 ] In 2015, over 143,000 people attended the three-day event which raised $60,000 for Nashville non-profits. [ 232 ]
A festival held in October, featuring readings, panels, and book signings. [ 233 ]
Award ceremony normally held in November at the Bridgestone Arena and televised to a national audience.

A parade running down Broadway on 11/11 at 11:11.11 am since 1951. Features include 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault), Tennessee National Guard, veterans from wars past and present, military plane fly-overs, tanks, motorcycles, first responder vehicles, marching bands and thousands of spectators. [ 234 ]
